commentary_title: VLGC rates collapse on weak Asian demand
commentary_summary: Subdued demand and narrowing US-Asia arbitrage slowed fixing activity lowering shipping rates | VLGC spot rates dropped 37% WoW on US-Japan route to an average $65.3 per tonne in the week ending 19 January | Weak petchem margins led to unplanned shutdowns in China, declining the operating rates to 67% | The number of laden vessels in China and India is lower, even after accounting for seasonality

commentary_title: VLGC rates rises on improving arbitrage
commentary_summary: US LPG prices decline as propane inventory build-up due to increased production | Widening arbitrage supports a rise in US VLGC fixtures for Asia | China's LPG demand improves with conclusion of lunar new moon holidays and favourable propane-naphtha spread | Spot rates increased 7% WoW on US-Japan route to an average of $94.12 per tonne in the week ending 16 February | VLGC passage through Panama Canal increases MoM in February

commentary_title: VLGC rates continue their recovery
commentary_summary: Spot rates on benchmark routes up 50% MoM ( AG-Japan at $79 per tonne, US-Japan at $137 per tonne) | Robust fixtures from the US pick-up rates but, arbitrage remains volatile | Lucrative premium in the West attracting vessels, in turn tightening availability in the East of Suez | Drewry LPG tonne-mile index up to 114.5 points this week as activity increases | VLGC transits through Panama Canal on the rise, a slight fall seen on COGH

commentary_title: LPG trade stable amid a volatile arbitrage
commentary_summary: Fixing activity to remain robust in the next week as the US-Asia price arbitrage gradually opens. | Congestion increased with more laden tonnage at anchor in China. | China's petchem sector to support LPG demand amid the start of new PDH plants. Further boost will be provided with improving PDH margins. | Meanwhile, seasonality will affect the Asian LPG demand from the rest of the sectors, pressurising rates. | The tonne-mile index rose to 124.1 points from 118.7 last week and has been increasing consecutively for the last six weeks with increased transits from COGH and the Panama Canal.

commentary_title: VLGC rates rise on favourable arbitrage
commentary_summary: VLGC spot rates rise 6% WoW on the US-Japan route to an average of $140.17 per tonne in the week ending 10 May | Improved US-Asia arbitrage and lower Saudi LPG prices aiding fixing activity and demand | Competition for VLGCs rises at the Panama Canal as LNGCs and containerships increase transits | Asian LPG demand is still under pressure given the persisting negative PDH margins | Ballast tonnage volume rises in the Atlantic as VLGCs opt to move to the West through COGH for higher earning; also squeezing vessel availability

commentary_title: VLGC transits improve with rise in Panama Canal slots
commentary_summary: Vessels underway in the West rising as ballast ships build up. | Vessels are opting for COGH for the ballast leg of the journey and moving towards the West to earn higher premiums. | Vessels moving to the west creating vessel tightness in the East. | Spot rates remained stable impacted muted spot demand from India.

commentary_title: US loadings affected by Hurricane Beryl
commentary_summary: US LPG prices increased despite the inventory build-up due to hurricane Beryl affecting vessel movement in US Gulf | A narrowing US-Asia price arbitrage weighed on the fixing activity impacting the spot rates | VLGC spot rates on the AG-Japan and US-Japan routes each declined 7% WoW, averaging $69.2 per tonne and $109.1 per tonne respectively. | Asian demand to be impacted by the arrival of monsoon and dismal PDH margins in China

commentary_title: VLGC rates under pressure on narrowing arbitrage
commentary_summary: VLGC transits through Panama increase as more slots become available. | US loadings impacted due to hurricane and Houston shipping channel closure. Consequently, laden tonnage falls in the Atlantic and Pacific. | VLGC spot rates on the AG-Japan route declined 9% WoW in the week ending 2nd August while it remained stable on the US-Japan and US-Europe routes. | Restart of PDH units after scheduled maintenance could increase operating rates; uncertainity revloves around petchem margins

commentary_title: VLGC rates rise on higher US fixtures
commentary_summary: US VLGC loadings rise as terminals resume spot cargo offers after clearing backlog from hurrican Beryl | Fixtures increased in the West with propane inventory build-up widening the US-Asia price arbitrage, resulting in US-Japan spot rates rising 17% WoW to average $116.15 per tonne. | Meanwhile, VLGC spot rates on the AG-Japan route surged 27% WoW to average $61.27 per tonne, with many fixture inquiries from India for September loadings. | China's LPG demand increased in August with the start of new PDH plants increasing the laden tonnage at anchor in China. | However, the persisting negative margins hold an uncertain outlook for operating run rates and the petchem sector.

commentary_title: VLGC rates weaken on lower Middle Eastern exports, increasing vessel availability in West
commentary_summary: VLGC transits rise through Cape of Good Hope; decline at the Panama Canal. | Fall in Middle Eastern exports incentivise owners to ballast vessels to the West. | Higher COGH transits improving tonne-mile demand; vessel build- up likely in the West. | No significant impact on US Gulf loadings from Hurricane Francine. | Spot rates declined 30% and 17% in the first half of the month on AG-Japan and US-Japan benchmark route.

commentary_title: Rates improve on higher loading in the US
commentary_summary: VLGC spot rates improving with easing congestion at US Gulf; backlog created due to hurricane delays clearing. | Limited activity in the East of Suez but fixtures look to increase on Indian demand ahead of festivals. | No major impact on LPG shipping so far due to the escalating Iran- Israel tensions in the Middle East. | A longer fixing window and narrowing US-Asia arbitrage expected to curb the rise in VLGC rates. | LPG demand in the Asian petchem sector expected to decline due to negative margins and competition from naphtha.

commentary_title: Falling tonne-mile demand deflating VLGC spot rates despite bump in Indian inquires
commentary_summary: Declining laden tonnage across the Indian, Atlantic, and Pacific oceans indicates a reduction in LPG trade along major routes. | Spot rates on AG-Japan fall 17% WoW while US-Japan fall 7%; Rates in the West could ease further as vessels compete for limited cargo. | Higher Indian inquiries for November deliveries to provide support; Delays at East coast ports due to cyclone Dana may lead to congestion. | Rising propane prices, driven by Israel-Iran tensions, are expected to decrease LPG demand east of Suez as petrochemical industry, especially in China, is likely to shift to naphtha.

commentary_title: VLGC spot rates improved with improved supply and rising inquiries from China and India
commentary_summary: The tonne mile index improving, backed up robust US and Middle East supply and increasing demand from India and China | Spot freight rates rose 2% WoW on AG-Japan and 8% WoW on US- Japan routes. | Low residential LPG prices in India raised laden tonnage in the Indian Ocean, and strong petchem demand despite negative margins did same in the Pacific. | Rates are expected to improve over Nov-Dec, with the majority of hurricane activity in USG now over. Vessel surplus to curb growth.

commentary_title: VLGC spot rates slump amidst weak Asian demand.
commentary_summary: Spot freight rates fell by 3% WoW on the AG-Japan route and by 2% WoW on the US-Japan route due to weak downstream demand in China. | Accordingly, the tonne miles index dropped by 3% WoW with a dismal trend expected over December. | Rising congestion at Indian LPG terminals to provide boost to VLGC rates in December. | US-Asia arbitrage could face volatility with High US terminal fees and lower Chinese petchem production easing Asian prices.

commentary_title: VLGCs start 2025 with rates firming as vessel availability tightens
commentary_summary: Higher loading in both- the US and the Middle East eases the available tonnage list; 15 VLGCs loaded from the US in the first week of 2025 | VLGC spot rates on the AG-Japan and US-Japan recovering from the holiday lull, yet down 4% and 1% WoW, respectively; Tonne-mile index up 2.6% | Robust Asian demand and fall in LPG prices to support trade. Expected increase in vessel loadings from the Middle East to lure shipowners to divert vessels to the East. | The US-Asia price arbitrage supported trade, but prices will be volatile as the US terminal capacity nears its limits.

commentary_title: VLGC earnings to remain under stress amid vessel oversupply.
commentary_summary: VLGC earnings on the benchmark US-Japan route fell 5% WoW while on AG-Japan route declined 13% WoW. | The recent winter storm in the US disrupted loadings at terminals, causing buildup of tonnage and exerted downward pressure on rates. | As vessels ballasted towards the Middle East to mitigate the situation, an oversupply near the Gulf pressurised spot rates on AG- Japan route. | This shift in export source impacted tonne-miles demand, resulting in a 7% WoW drop in the tonne-miles index to 116.6 points. | Laden tonnage at anchor in China decreased sharply this week as the country entered the Lunar New year holidays.

commentary_title: VLGC earnings to remain under stress amid vessel oversupply and weak demand
commentary_summary: VLGC earnings on the benchmark US-Japan route fell 4% WoW while on AG-Japan route declined 6% WoW. | Increased vessel availability amid weak demand from India and China exerted downward pressure on rates. Low Laden tonnage at anchor in China confirms this trend. | Accordingly, tonne miles index declined 4.5% reaching 113.6 points, indicating reduction in long-haul trade. | Normalisation of red sea crisis will have minimal impact on LPG trade. However, petchem trade on Europe-Asia route can see marginal improvement.

commentary_title: VLGC earnings to improve slightly on improving Indian demand
commentary_summary: VLGC earnings showcased stability on the benchmark US-Japan and AG-Japan routes, despite a 4.3% increase in tonne miles demand. | The tonne miles demand increased because of robust Indian demand. However, vessel surplus dampened recovery in rates. | Congestion at Indian terminals rising due to the higher imports, created delays as indicated by the increase in laden tonnage at anchor. | Conversely, the indicator showcased decline in China as the country’s LPG imports remained subdued.

commentary_title: VLGC earnings to dwindle amid weak demand, higher vessel availability
commentary_summary: VLGC spot rates on the benchmark US-Japan route and AG-Japan route fell 1% and 8% WoW respectively. | Drewry's LPG tonne mile Index also registered a 6% WoW fall to 117.6 points, indicative of reduced trade | Ballast tonnage indicator for China surged, suggesting a rise in 'for order' vessels in the region | Meanwhile, laden tonnage at anchor indicator for India declined, signalling easing congestion amid easing LPG demand

commentary_title: VLGC earnings waver amid US-China tariff war uncertainity
commentary_summary: VLGC spot rates on the benchmark US-Japan route and AG-Japan route rose 15% and 25% WoW, respectively, after falling to $86 per tonne and $39.5 per tonne last week. | Uncertainty caused by the US-China tariff war led Chinese buyers to rush for alternative supplies, boosting spot rates on AG-Japan routes. | Further, tonne mile demand created by diversion of US cargoes towards India and Indonesia resulted in increased spot rates on US- Japan route and led to 3% WoW rise in Drewry's LPG tonne mile index. | The Atlantic ballast tonnage indicator remained high for two consecutive weeks as VLGCs positioned near the US coast to capitalise on widening US Asia price arbitrage.

commentary_title: VLGC earnings improve as trade pattern changes
commentary_summary: Spot rates on the benchmark US-Japan and AG-Japan route rose 2% and 9% WoW, respectively, reaching $104 and $53 per tonne in week 19. | Rates on AG-Japan surged as China switched to the Middle East amid US-China tariff escalations. | The recent de-escalation involving retaliatory tariffs on LPG falling to 10% from 125% earlier likely to boost US-China trade. | Drewry's LPG tonne miles index registered a 7% WoW rise as Asian demand showed sighs of recovery. | Drewry's laden tonnage indicator showcases vessels moving towards US for loading, indicating another trade pattern change.

commentary_title: VLGC TCE at $50,000 pd but demand uncertainty to break the rally
commentary_summary: Spot rates on the benchmark US-Japan and AG-Japan declined 2% and 7% WoW, respectively, after peaking at $113.5 and $67.2 per tonne in week 21. | Repositioning of vessels from the Middle East to the USGC created temporary tightness, impacting rates. | Uncertainty in the market keeps buyers in a "wait-and-see" mode, fixtures lacklustre out of the US. | Despite volatility in rates, Drewry's LPG tonne miles index remained stable. | Meanwhile, Drewry’s Laden tonnage at anchor indicator for the Pacific Basin showed an uptick, reflecting an increase in demand from Far East Asia, particularly China.

commentary_title: Israel-Iran tensions raise VLGC rates
commentary_summary: Spot rates on the AG Japan route spiked 19% WoW, reaching $85.1 per tonne, as the tensions in the Persian Gulf escalated. | GPS jamming near Iran and vessel bunching in the Gulf of Oman caused variation in the vessel supply data. | This disruption led to a spike in laden tonnage at anchor across the Indian Ocean. | Meanwhile, tonne-miles index rose 8% WoW, reaching 132.8 points as US LPG exports increased following de-escalation in tariff tensions.

commentary_title: VLGC rates normalises amid easing Panama congestion and rising vessel availability
commentary_summary: Spot rates on the AG-Japan and US-Japan routes declined by 7% and 5% WoW, respectively, as increased vessel availability reversed the prior bullish trend. | Easing Panama Canal congestion is resulting in increased VLGC transits, increasing vessel availability. | Low Asian delivered prices and narrowing US-Asia arbitrage also pressurise spot rates. | Meanwhile, Drewry's laden tonnage at anchor in China indicator rose, signalling LPG import recovery amid rising PDH demand. | Other factors—reduced war risk premium and 90-day extension of US- China tariff pause—has reasserted supply-demand fundamentals and led to downward movement in rates.

commentary_title: VLGC rates ease but maintain good levels
commentary_summary: Spot rates on the AG-Japan and US-Japan routes declined by 6% and 2% WoW, respectively, amid increased fixtures absorbing vessels | China's LPG demand is projected to fall, leading to increased vessel availability. Japan and South Korean import demand muted despite open arbitrage. | Drewry's laden tonnage at anchor- China indicator showcases a rise in vessels waiting to discharge following the second tariff pause between US and China. | Meanwhile, Drewry's LPG tonne-mile Index improved due to the surge in US-China LPG trade. | The impact of the USTR regulations on LPG shipping remains insignificant with under 10% of VLGCs affected, already being reprogrammed away from US trade.

commentary_title: VLGC spot rates normalise amid easing demand and increased tonnage availability
commentary_summary: Spot rates on the AG-Japan and US-Japan routes declined by 7% and 4% WoW, respectively, amid fading demand and increased vessel availability. | Demand concerns have again hit the LPG market as China's LPG imports decline due to weak petchem margins. Meanwhile, Japan and South Korea's weak residential demand impacted their imports. | Buyers remain cautious on 2026 term volumes amid weak fundamentals, leading to lower contract renewals and inspiring decline in Saudi CP benchmarks. Elevated spot rates in prior months have further compressed petchem margins due to high landed cost, dampening downstream demand. | Drewry’s laden tonnage at anchor (China) indicator fell, indicating the end of China’s restocking phase and the onset of a low-demand 4Q25. | Additionally, proposed China's port fees on US-linked vessels and potential USTR regulations could bifurcate the VLGC market, forcing US- or China-linked tonnage to reallocate away from the US-China trade.

commentary_title: Vessel repositioning drives uptick in VLGC spot rates
commentary_summary: Spot rates on the AG-Japan and US-Japan routes rose 26% and 13% WoW, respectively, driven by fleet reshuffing following 1-year pause on retaliatory tariffs, USTR and the tightened vessel supply. | The spike is supply-led, while demand remains weak amid poor Asian petchem margins. Declining laden tonnage at anchor in India and China confirms the trend. | Weak demand fundamentals and ample supply have already anchored a decline in Saudi CP benchmarks narrowing US-Middle East arbitrage. | LPG shipping to face volatile period if Middle East-Asia flows improve on sliding LPG prices, which will reduce tonne-mile demand and cap VLGC spot rates.

commentary_title: VLGC tonne-mile demand rises despite subdued spot market activity
commentary_summary: Drewry’s tonne-mile index rose further from the previous week, indicating increasing share of laden VLGCs in both the East and West. | Spot market activity remained subdued as weak Asian buying interest limited enquiries and fixtures. | Meanwhile, stronger Middle East demand tightened Atlantic vessel availability and brought additional July US Gulf cargoes to market. | Freight rates in the East continued to command a strong premium over ex- US Gulf routes, supported by robust Middle East loading activity. | Meanwhile, regional oil companies increasingly used their own vessels for Strait of Hormuz transits.

commentary_title: VLGC spot market holds firm despite declining tonne-mile demand
commentary_summary: The tonne-mile index continued to decline, reaching 109. | At the same time, the share of laden VLGCs fell in the East but increased in the West. | Tight vessel availability in the West kept the VLGC spot market firm throughout the week. | Meanwhile, rates in the East remained strong despite renewed uncertainty following the resumption of hostilities in the Middle East Gulf. | Although demand for vessels willing to enter the Middle East Gulf stayed healthy, the pool of eligible ships continued to shrink.

commentary_title: VLGC market activity remains muted as tonne-miles index falls
commentary_summary: The tonne-miles index continued its downward trend this week, falling to 95.1, while the share of laden vessels declined in both the East and West. | The VLGC spot market was relatively quiet, with challenging trading conditions and the summer holiday period limiting fixture activity. | In the West, rates eased slightly but remained firm for some routes, while charterers remained cautious due to volatile arbitrage economics. | Although the end-August and early-September vessel positions remain tight, elevated Panama Canal auction costs have encouraged charterers to postpone fixing. | Meanwhile, the Eastern market saw very little activity this week as uncertainty surrounding the ongoing Middle East conflict continued to weigh on sentiment.

commentary_title: Panama Canal delays and rising Western rates drive VLGC spot market
commentary_summary: The tonne-mile index dropped to 92.3 in Week 35 after rising to reach 99.6 the previous week. | Meanwhile, the share of laden vessels shifted slightly, declining in the East and rising in the West, though both week-over-week changes were marginal. | The spot market in the West stabilized slightly after the previous week's gains, which were driven by fewer available ships and growing Panama Canal delays tied to Super El Nino expectations. | Higher canal auction costs and reduced transit slots from September continued to push rates up from Week 34. | Despite these Western gains and a minor drop in the East's laden vessel share, Eastern spot activity remained quiet, apart from Vadinar fixtures.

commentary_title: Tonne-mile index rises as October availability tightens
commentary_summary: The tonne-mile index rose to 103.0 this week from 96.4 previously. | West market activity continued to remain subdued amid industry events in London and Singapore. | However, several fixtures were concluded for the last two weeks of October, while the September position list has cleared. | The last two weeks of October will face tight availability of vessels. | East market activity also remained subdued, although a spot vessel was fixed for STS Vadinar for mid-September dates.
